_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
A competing updater previously closed a running simulator experiment through Windows RestartManager. Automatic updates now wait for other installed Smart Cuff Python processes and the operational GUI mutex, use NOCLOSEAPPLICATIONS, serialize update transactions, and complete recording/acquisition cleanup before installation. Closing an active sweep keeps it running and shows “Stop sweep, then close”; Windows shutdown retains the existing stop-and-save path.

The live PID diagnostic also rejects invalid pulse-cadence fit bounds and contains numerical display errors so valve/pump status and telemetry processing continue. SysID band checks, calibrated mmHg/L/min recordings, multi-protocol simulator plans and MAP-versus-measured-hold diagnostics from the previous bundle are retained.

Focused shutdown/update and diagnostic regressions, smoke and layout checks passed on both branches. This host-only update retains the qualified branch firmware and existing controller settings. Controller/MAP/SysID research candidates are excluded. MAP reference derived from SP/DP is not an independent arterial measurement.
Default retains five presets and followup-288 firmware.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
